lessons.title: What happens when someone logs in?
objectives: Trace a login request through real source, step by step.
Predict what fails when AuthService.login stops calling SessionStore.create, then check against a recorded test run.
Repair the connection and explain why the failure was not local.

steps.caption: This is auth-service, a small TypeScript service written as a sample for EXPLODE. Its graph was built from the actual source.
Pull it apart to see its 8 subsystems.
steps.hint: Pinch with both hands and pull them apart, or press Explode.

steps.caption: What happens when someone logs in? Press Trace Login to follow the request.
steps.hint: The Trace Login button is in the panel next to you.

steps.caption: Each of the 9 steps exists in the source. Select one and open its evidence to see the lines.
steps.hint: Select any glowing part, then press Evidence.

steps.caption: Suppose AuthService.login stopped calling SessionStore.create. Which step would fail first? Point at it.

on_enter.question: If AuthService.login stops calling SessionStore.create, which step fails first?

steps.hint: Steps before the missing call still run. Look for the first step that would no longer be called.

feedback.correct: Right. SessionStore.create never runs, so no session is created and no token is signed.
feedback.incorrect: Not quite. Steps before the missing call still run. The failure starts at SessionStore.create and spreads to everything after it.

steps.caption: Now test it. Unplug the call from AuthService.login to SessionStore.create. The real repository is not changed.
steps.hint: Select the highlighted connection, then press Unplug.

steps.caption: Observed: with this call removed, 3 of 10 tests failed in a test run recorded when this content was built. Open the evidence to see which.
Reconnect the call. Three sockets are offered, and only one is right.
steps.hint: AuthService.login needs to create the session before anything can be signed.

steps.caption: The failure was not local. One missing call stopped everything after it on the login path, and the tests caught it.
